newsitem.title: UK: Clarke fully backs UK EMU position - Major's office.
newsitem.headline: Clarke fully backs UK EMU position - Major's office.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke fully supports the British government's policy on a single currency, as does Foreign Office minister Sir Nicholas Bonsor, Prime Minister John Major's office said on Tuesday.

The spokesman was speaking after Bonsor told BBC radio that Clarke was out of line with the vast majority of the Conservative party, and with government policy, when he said it would be pathetic if Britain were to wait and see how a European single currency developed before deciding whether to join.
"The prime minister has made it clear that all ministers must adhere fully to the position agreed in cabinet.
"The Chancellor of the Exchequer fully supports the policy and believes his views have been misrepresented," the spokesman said.
Bonsor, meanwhile, had given his interview based on press reports of Clarke's comments and accepts he was mistaken. "He fully supports the government's position," the spokesman added.

The comments appeared to be an attempt to draw a line under a fierce row that has rocked the Conservative party less than two weeks before its annual conference and that resulted on Tuesday in financial rumours, denied as nonsense by the Treasury, that Clarke had resigned.
Asked whether Major still had confidence in Clarke, the prime minister's spokesman said, "Self-evidently all ministers have the prime minister's confidence."
Major's office said the government had an agreed policy on when a decision on a single currency should be taken and that many issues of importance to Britain remain to be resolved.
These would affect Britain "whether we remain in a single currency or not and it is right that Britain should play its full role in the negotiations", the spokesman added.
